headline: Steady growth, but a higher tax rate keeps net income flat
summary_short: AIT's fiscal Q3 (three months ended March 31, 2026, labeled FY2026 Q1 on this shard) net sales rose 7.3% y/y to $1,251.5M as both segments grew organically, but a jump in the effective tax rate to 26.2% from 21.6% held net income flat at $99.8M even as diluted EPS still rose 3.1% to $2.65 on a lower share count.
summary_long: Sales grew 7.3% y/y ($84.7M) to $1,251.5M, with 6.0% organic growth from higher volumes and price across both segments; acquisitions and FX added the rest. Operating income rose 6.6% to $137.9M on incremental gross profit, though margin slipped to 11.0% from 11.1% on higher LIFO expense and compensation-driven SD&A growth. The effective tax rate jumped to 26.2% from 21.6% on discrete prior-year items and a smaller R&D credit, leaving net income roughly flat at $99.8M; diluted EPS still rose 3.1% to $2.65 on a 3.0% lower share count from buybacks. Cash fell to $171.6M after $236.4M of nine-month buybacks and $207.0M of debt repayment. Management expects a full-year fiscal-2026 effective tax rate of 23.0%-24.0%; no other guidance given.

drivers.explanation: Sales rose $84.7M (7.3%): $69.7M organic (6.0%) from higher volumes (~$40.0M) and price in both segments, plus $5.5M from acquisitions and $9.5M favorable FX.
Both segments grew operating income on higher revenues and, for Engineered Solutions, incremental gross profit on volumes, partly offset by higher SD&A from compensation costs.
Tracks operating income's rise; the filing does not separately discuss EBITDA as a distinct metric.
Higher operating income was offset by a higher effective tax rate (26.2% vs 21.6%) from discrete prior-year tax items and a smaller R&D credit benefit.
Net income was roughly flat, but basic weighted-average shares fell as the Company repurchased stock, lifting per-share income.
Diluted shares fell 3.0% y/y on buybacks while net income was roughly flat, producing the 3.1% EPS increase the release cites.
Margin held roughly flat (30.4% vs 30.5%) as higher LIFO expense (-0.3ppt) was offset by favorable mix from Engineered Solutions growth; absolute profit rose with sales.
Rose in line with the 7.3% sales increase; LIFO expense increased to $5.6M from $2.2M a year ago, pressuring cost of sales.
Followed operating income's rise, partly offset by higher net interest expense ($2.4M vs $0.9M) from lower interest income on lower cash balances.
Not explained in the release; the segment reconciliation table shows both Service Center and Engineered Solutions spending less than the prior-year quarter.
Nine-month operating cash flow of $319.1M was outweighed by $236.4M of buybacks, $207.0M of net revolver repayment, and dividends paid.
The Company used $207.0M to pay down revolver borrowings after its interest-rate swap matured in January 2026, within a new five-year $900M facility entered in October 2025.
The $18.0M current portion reflects revolver borrowings the Company intends to repay within twelve months, per the debt footnote; none was classified as current a year ago.
Retained-earnings growth from trailing net income outweighed the increase in treasury stock from $236.4M of nine-month buybacks, per the equity statement.
The Company repurchased 897,115 shares for $236.4M over nine months and the Board authorized a new 3.0 million-share buyback in April 2026.

Management points to broad-based volume growth, positive price contribution, and rising industrial-production indices (MCU/PMI/MIP) through March 2026, offset at the net-income line by a higher effective tax rate.
